blindSourceSummaries: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (anti-bot access-denied interstitial); per the country dossier this 16 July 2026 foreign-wire report covers the convicted far-right prisoner placed in a men's prison despite a legal gender change - the event that drove three other units to launch a federal-council initiative to tighten the national self-determination law. Framework-level for every unit, since prison administration and registry offices are state/province competences.

Constitutional-law blog essay (18 March 2026) on how units are rewriting prison-execution codes for trans inmates: a majority of the country's 16 states have replaced placement rules unchanged since the 1970s (one unit's new rules took effect 1 March 2026, following several others), all anchoring placement to the civil-registry sex entry, which the author argues is constitutionally avoidable (self-declaration would suffice) and partly doubtful. A resident-detention analysis applying nationwide, not a visitor-facing finding for any single unit.

News report (23 August 2023) on the country's prisons and trans inmates: a transgender climate activist, a trans woman whose legal sex is male, faces placement in a men's prison; the prison-staff union's federal chair says men's prisons are inadequately prepared and understaffed (some 2,000 officer shortage; ~60,000 inmates in nearly 200 facilities); prisons are state/province jurisdiction and some units run special facilities or guidelines. National framework context for all 16 units.
